gaps.sentence: The report ___ have been finished yesterday; the deadline was missed.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have been finished' — it was expected but did not happen.

gaps.sentence: The theatre was completely empty, so the performance ___ have been very popular.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' draws a negative conclusion from evidence: can't have been.

gaps.sentence: He ___ be at work — I've just seen him at the beach.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' expresses something the evidence rules out.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have lied to the police — it was a serious mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' plus the participle criticizes a past action: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: You ___ use my office while I am on holiday.
It ___ be the postman — he has already been this morning.
gaps.hint: ruled out by what already happened
gaps.explanation: Evidence that rules something out uses 'can't': can't be.

gaps.sentence: It is Saturday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early.
gaps.hint: an absence of obligation at weekends
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' shows there is no obligation: don't have to get up.

gaps.sentence: We ___ book a table — the restaurant is never full on Mondays.
gaps.hint: the action is unnecessary, use needn't
gaps.explanation: When something is unnecessary, use 'needn't' or 'don't have to': needn't book.
